words.definition: the place or type of environment in which an organism normally lives
words.example: A mangrove swamp is the habitat of many salt-tolerant species.

words.definition: a non-living physical or chemical component of the environment
words.example: Temperature is an abiotic factor that affects species distribution.

words.definition: the range of an environmental factor within which an organism can survive and reproduce
words.example: A species may occupy only habitats within its temperature range of tolerance.

words.definition: an environmental factor that restricts population size, growth or distribution
words.example: Low light can be a limiting factor for plants beneath a dense canopy.

words.definition: a line or strip along which organisms or environmental variables are sampled
words.example: A belt transect can show how plant distribution changes across a shore.

words.definition: a diverse marine ecosystem built largely from calcium-carbonate structures produced by corals
words.example: Coral reefs usually develop in warm, clear, shallow seas.

words.definition: the concentration of dissolved salts in water or soil
words.example: Salinity influences which organisms can live in an estuary.

words.definition: the degree to which light can pass through water without being scattered or absorbed
words.example: High water clarity allows light to reach photosynthetic organisms at greater depth.

words.definition: a large ecological region characterized by climate and dominant vegetation
words.example: Temperature and precipitation strongly influence the distribution of biomes.

words.definition: a warm, wet biome with high rainfall and dense evergreen vegetation
words.example: Tropical rainforests support very high species diversity.

words.definition: a forest biome of mid-latitudes with moderate temperatures and seasonal conditions
words.example: Many temperate forests contain deciduous trees.

words.definition: a cold northern forest biome dominated mainly by coniferous trees
words.japanese: タイガ・亜寒帯針葉樹林
words.example: Taiga occurs across large areas of Canada and Eurasia.

words.definition: a biome dominated by grasses with relatively few trees
words.example: Grassland plants are adapted to grazing, fire and seasonal drought.

words.definition: a cold treeless biome with a short growing season and often permanently frozen subsoil
words.example: Tundra vegetation is generally low-growing because of cold and wind.

words.definition: a very dry biome with high temperatures and sparse vegetation
words.example: Hot-desert organisms have adaptations that reduce water loss.

words.definition: a plant adapted to survive in environments where water is scarce
words.example: Cacti are xerophytes with features that conserve water.

words.definition: a heritable feature that improves survival or reproduction under particular environmental conditions
words.example: Thick fur is an environmental adaptation in some cold-climate mammals.

words.definition: the set of resources, conditions and interactions that define how a species lives and functions in an ecosystem
words.example: A species' ecological niche includes its food sources, habitat and interactions.

words.definition: an organism that cannot survive or grow in the presence of oxygen
words.example: Some bacteria are obligate anaerobes and are harmed by oxygen.

words.definition: an organism that can use oxygen when available but can also live without it
words.example: Yeast can behave as a facultative anaerobe.

words.definition: an organism that requires oxygen for cellular respiration and growth
words.example: An obligate aerobe depends on oxygen as part of its metabolism.

words.definition: an organism that makes organic compounds from inorganic carbon using light or chemical energy
words.example: Green plants are autotrophs that fix carbon dioxide.

words.definition: an autotroph that uses light energy to synthesize organic compounds
words.example: Most plants are photoautotrophs.

words.definition: an organism that obtains organic molecules by consuming or absorbing material produced by other organisms
words.example: Animals are heterotrophs.

words.definition: a mode of heterotrophic nutrition involving ingestion and internal digestion of solid or liquid food
words.example: Humans obtain nutrients by holozoic nutrition.

words.definition: an organism that digests dead organic matter externally and absorbs the soluble products
words.example: Many fungi are saprotrophs.

words.definition: an organism, mainly bacteria or fungi, that breaks down dead organic material and recycles nutrients
words.example: Decomposers release mineral nutrients back into ecosystems.

words.definition: an organism that ingests dead organic fragments and digests them internally
words.example: Earthworms are detritivores that consume dead plant material.

words.definition: a heterotrophic organism that obtains energy and nutrients by feeding on other organisms or organic matter
words.example: A rabbit is a primary consumer in many grassland food chains.

words.definition: the way an organism obtains and processes food or nutrients
words.example: Filter feeding is one feeding mode used by aquatic animals.

words.definition: the principle that species with effectively identical niches cannot coexist indefinitely in the same place
words.example: Competitive exclusion can occur when two species depend on exactly the same limiting resource.

words.definition: the full range of environmental conditions and resources a species could use in the absence of biotic restrictions
words.example: A species' fundamental niche may be broader than the area it actually occupies.

words.definition: the part of a species' fundamental niche actually occupied after competition and other biotic interactions
words.example: Competition can reduce a species' realized niche.

words.definition: an organism capable of using both autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition
words.example: Some protists are mixotrophs that photosynthesize but can also ingest food.

words.definition: a domain of prokaryotic organisms genetically and biochemically distinct from bacteria
words.example: Many archaea live in ordinary environments as well as extreme habitats.

words.definition: the number, type and arrangement of teeth in an animal
words.example: Dentition can reveal adaptations to different diets.

words.definition: a structural, physiological or behavioural feature that improves feeding on plants
words.example: Broad grinding teeth are a herbivore adaptation in many mammals.

words.definition: a feature that improves an organism's ability to detect, capture or consume prey
words.example: Forward-facing eyes can be a predator adaptation that improves depth perception.

words.definition: a feature that reduces the chance of being detected, captured or eaten by predators
words.example: Camouflage is a common prey adaptation.

words.definition: a plant that grows on another plant for physical support without taking nutrients directly from its tissues
words.example: Many orchids are epiphytes that grow on rainforest tree branches.
